defaultRoutingPolicy.reason: Rule-core drivers prove reusable mechanics and should deepen a rule module before a battle subject consumes them.
Selected-identity/catalog drivers wait until their generic runtime substrate exists; authored identity is not a production dispatch mechanism.
Unlisted battle drivers need a short derivability record before they become reducer-spine diagnostic tasks.

qntFacts: packages/battle-runtime/battle-runtime-reducer-spine-contract.mbt.qnt models the reducer lifecycle from battle start through act discovery, subject hole/fill resolution, turn advancement, and reducer-owned resource/vital projections.

diagnosticBatches.purpose: Route selected focused battle drivers through the shared BattleState reducer surface instead of slice-local replay helpers.

entries.subjectFamily: slot spell with target allocation and damage roll fills
entries.durableStateOwner: BattleState owns current actor, turn action resource, spell-slot expenditure, and target Hit Points; the adapter owns only replay evidence.
entries.acceptanceCondition: Target replay evidence shows Magic Missile allocation and damage actions resolved through the shared reducer entrypoints and battle-owned state fields.

qntFacts: packages/battle-runtime/battle-runtime-magic-missile.mbt.qnt exposes SpellTargetAllocation then SpellDamageRoll and asserts target HP, death flag, action availability, multiattack dispatch count, and Sneak Attack turn use projection.

packages/battle-runtime/battle-runtime-reducer-spine-contract.mbt.qnt already models SlotSpellSubject discovery, spell target fills, damage fills, committed spell-slot use, and battle-owned Hit Points through the reducer surface.
rawDomainFacts: .references/srd-5.2.1/Spells/Gaining-and-Casting.md#Spell Slots establishes slot expenditure on cast.
.references/srd-5.2.1/Playing-the-Game.md#Hit Points and UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md#Hit Points and Death establish BattleState-owned Hit Point projection.
UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md#Action Lifecycle names subject, hole, fill, and resolution vocabulary.

entries.durableStateOwner: BattleState owns subject frontier progress and spell resource effects; ordering-error labels remain reducer result facts, not adapter state.
entries.acceptanceCondition: Target replay evidence reuses the existing Magic-action and spell-slot ownership instead of introducing a local save-gated ordering island.

qntFacts: packages/battle-runtime/battle-runtime-save-gated-spell-ordering.mbt.qnt exposes target or area, Saving Throw outcome, condition choice, and damage dice frontiers.
packages/battle-runtime/battle-runtime-save-gated-spell-ordering.qnt is the semantic core for save-gated spell hole-frontier order.
rawDomainFacts: .references/srd-5.2.1/Playing-the-Game.md#Saving Throws defines Saving Throw resolution as effect resistance.
UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md#Spellcasting and UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md#Action Lifecycle provide domain vocabulary.
blockers: If the target engine has not yet represented Magic-action spell subjects or slot ownership from the Magic Missile route, record a source/target blocker instead of building a driver-local ordering module.

entries.subjectFamily: Hit Point restoration frontier ordering and zero-HP cleanup
entries.durableStateOwner: BattleState owns restored target Hit Points and zero-Hit-Point lifecycle cleanup; the healing frontier does not own a duplicate HP ledger.
entries.acceptanceCondition: Target replay evidence adds HP restoration through the battle-owned HP lifecycle and keeps spell target/distribution fills as reducer subject progress.

qntFacts: packages/battle-runtime/battle-runtime-hit-point-restoration-ordering.mbt.qnt exposes spell healing target choice/list, healing roll, feature healing-pool distribution, and zero-HP cleanup projections.
packages/battle-runtime/battle-runtime-hit-point-restoration-ordering.qnt is the semantic core for restoration frontier order.
rawDomainFacts: .references/srd-5.2.1/Playing-the-Game.md#Healing and .references/srd-5.2.1/Rules-Glossary.md#Hit Points define Hit Point restoration.
.references/srd-5.2.1/Playing-the-Game.md#Dropping to 0 Hit Points and UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md#Hit Points and Death define zero-HP lifecycle effects.
blockers: If the target engine has no battle-owned HP lifecycle substrate yet, implement that substrate first and record the durable field derivability before routing this driver.

entries.durableStateOwner: BattleState owns target Hit Points, Stable, Unconscious, Dead, and death-save counters; the adapter owns only sampled roll evidence.
entries.acceptanceCondition: Target replay evidence routes Death Saving Throw discovery/fill through turn advancement or subject resolution using the same HP lifecycle owner as damage and healing.

qntFacts: packages/battle-runtime/battle-runtime-death-saving-throw.mbt.qnt samples natural 1, ordinary failure, ordinary success, and natural 20 outcomes over the DeathSavingThrow hole.
packages/battle-runtime/battle-runtime-hit-points.qnt and packages/shared-algebras/proofs/rule-core/zero-hit-point-lifecycle.qnt own the copied reusable death-save and zero-HP lifecycle facts.

entries.durableStateOwner: BattleState owns concentrating source, active Spell Effect instances, and teardown before the next command; no adapter-local concentration ledger is allowed.
entries.acceptanceCondition: Target replay evidence proves failed damage save, voluntary end, and replacement Concentration teardown through one durable Concentration owner.

packages/battle-runtime/battle-runtime-concentration.qnt is the semantic owner for Concentration break facts.
